teams.synopsis: Still the top team, and the bench depth says the BYE weeks won't be a problem.
teams.blurb: Maintaining brevity, another fantastic week secures the top spot for this team. With solid bench depth featuring <mark class="hl-player">Thomas</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Downs</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Hubbard</mark>, this team is well-prepared to handle bye weeks and continue its impressive performance. Overall, the team's consistency and strength make it a top contender for the championship.

teams.synopsis: Quietly effective without a single trade — injuries aside, this team can outperform anyone at full strength.
teams.blurb: Gorman has been quietly effective in fantasy management thus far. Despite not making any trades, this team was well-constructed during the draft. Injuries, such as those to <mark class="hl-player">Deebo</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Kyren</mark>, have posed challenges, but when the team is at full strength, it has the potential to outperform any other team in the league. The second half of the season looks promising, and Gorman may have a shot at winning his first PFFL championship.

teams.synopsis: A third loss in five weeks reveals some vulnerability — but D/ST and K alone are contributing 22.5 a week.
teams.blurb: Carmine's team has slipped to the third spot in the rankings after suffering its third loss in the last five weeks, revealing its vulnerability once more. However, this team remains a formidable contender with one of the most star-studded lineups by name value alone. Impressively, Carmine's team has consistently scored no less than 100 points per week. Notably, his defense and kicker have contributed an average of 22.5 points per week, a significant lead over the runner-up in that category. While this may suggest some degree of luck in the first half of the season, it underscores the team's strength.

teams.synopsis: The biggest climber this week after a self-described 'career week' — Kelce, Harris, and Etienne all delivered.
teams.blurb: Aidan's team is the biggest climber in the rankings this week, and it's high time the squad gets the recognition it deserves. With what manager Ryan McQuaid called a 'career week,' the team put up a remarkable performance, leading to a notable shift in Aidan's ranking. The week saw standout performances, including the anticipated dominance of <mark class="hl-player">Travis Kelce</mark>, a strong week from <mark class="hl-player">Najee Harris</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Travis Etienne</mark> maintaining his status as a top-five RB. Given the team's impressive production and record, it's expected to remain a strong position in the rankings throughout the second half of the season.

teams.synopsis: Missing his RB1 and still put up 108 — three 134+ point weeks say the ceiling is among the league's best.
teams.blurb: Consistently ranked among the top five teams in the PFFL, Cole's squad is well-regarded as a competitive force in the league. In the previous week, the team posted 108 points in a loss to the only 6-1 team in the league, all while missing their RB1, <mark class="hl-player">Derrick Henry</mark>. Despite this setback, Cole's team has the potential to be the best in the league, evident from three remarkable weeks with 134+ points this season. To solidify its status as a front-runner for the 2023 PFFL championship, it's crucial for the team to maintain a higher level of consistency.

teams.synopsis: The third-most points on average all season — Chase and Diggs keep this team dangerous every week.
teams.blurb: Throughout the PFFL's 4th season, Brandon's team has maintained a consistent position as one of the top-performing teams, averaging the third-most points scored. A standout element is the dynamic wide receiver duo of <mark class="hl-player">Chase</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Diggs</mark>, who keep Brandon competitive in any matchup and provide significant upside. Despite a slight dip in performance — two weeks of 104 points following a major trade with Baylen — the team still maintains its overall strength and remains a prime candidate for the PFFL championship, with Brandon considered a lock for the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: One of the season's biggest turnaround stories takes a small step back — the WR trio remains elite.
teams.blurb: Baylen's team has been one of the standout stories of the 2023 PFFL season, showing significant improvement since its disappointing Week 1 performance. However, as the season reaches its midpoint, the team takes a step back to the 7th spot. While the team lacks high-profile name-value players, the majority of its roster has performed at an elite level this season. A trio of <mark class="hl-player">Thielen</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Meyers</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Hollywood</mark> has emerged as one of the top three wide receiver groups in the league. Meanwhile, <mark class="hl-player">Stroud</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">LaPorta</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Pacheco</mark> have all ranked among the top ten at their respective positions.

teams.synopsis: A solid 118 points without Breece Hall or Jefferson — the IR designation still adds WR2-level value.
teams.blurb: Ryan's team has moved up a spot in the rankings this week, despite a loss in Week 7. The team's solid output of 118 points, achieved without key players like <mark class="hl-player">Breece Hall</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Justin Jefferson</mark>, contributed to this rise. While the situation with Jefferson remains uncertain, having him on the IR spot still adds WR2-level value to the team. The upcoming Week 8 matchup against an injury-affected team will be crucial in assessing Ryan's playoff potential, particularly the team's scoring performance.

teams.synopsis: Two 125+ point weeks have this team climbing — even the D/ST and kicker are pulling their weight.
teams.blurb: Andrew's team has moved up two spots this week to secure the 9th position in the rankings, just outside the top eight. This ascent is due to the team producing two weeks with 125+ points in 2023. Despite still being in the bottom five in points scored throughout the season, Andrew's team ranks in the top three for points scored exclusively by defense and kicker each week — a testament to the impact of those positions, even though he's spoken against them recently. While the team has faced underwhelming performances from players like <mark class="hl-player">Josh Jacobs</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Jerry Jeudy</mark>, it's expected to remain a competitive opponent in the second half of the season.

teams.synopsis: The week's biggest faller — the backfield is thin, but Nico Collins' return offers some hope.
teams.blurb: Deniz experienced the most significant drop in Week 7, falling from the 7th to the 10th spot in the rankings. This was primarily due to his starting running backs potentially being <mark class="hl-player">Jerick McKinnon</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Jaleel McLaughlin</mark> for Week 8, which isn't ideal. Additionally, the recent poor performance of <mark class="hl-player">Davante Adams</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Amari Cooper</mark> has contributed to the team's struggles in recent weeks. However, Deniz has reasons to be hopeful, with <mark class="hl-player">Nico Collins</mark> returning and <mark class="hl-player">David Montgomery</mark> eyeing a Week 8 comeback. Currently holding a 3-4 record, it might be a bumpy road ahead, but there's still an expectation of a playoff push in the second half of the season.

teams.synopsis: Stuck in the #11-13 range for a month, but the Gibbs and Waller arrivals could change that.
teams.blurb: Max has found himself in the #11-#13 ranking range for the past four weeks, reflecting his team's underwhelming performance during that stretch. However, the arrivals of <mark class="hl-player">Jahmyr Gibbs</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Darren Waller</mark>, along with the return of injured players (assuming <mark class="hl-player">Tank Dell</mark> plays this week), have bolstered his team's outlook. Up to this point, weak quarterback and wide receiver production has hindered Max's chances of making the 2023 PFFL playoffs. If these positions can improve, Max could see his rankings rise again in Week 8.

teams.synopsis: Two wins in a row, but still stuck outside the playoff picture — Tee Higgins needs to step up.
teams.blurb: Anthony's team remains in the bottom three for another week, and there hasn't been much movement in the rankings. As we reach the midway point of the season, it appears Anthony is on the outskirts of the playoff picture, despite winning two weeks in a row. To contend for a championship in 2023, Anthony will need key players like <mark class="hl-player">Tee Higgins</mark> to step up. While it might be advisable to keep an eye on this team for potential trades, Anthony's recent victories may lead him to keep the current roster intact and take another shot in Week 8.

teams.synopsis: A top-7 Points For team stuck at 1-6 — if he and Ryan had swapped schedules, the records would flip entirely.
teams.blurb: It's painful to watch a team that started the season strong in points have such a poor record at the midway point. Ben's team has consistently ranked in the top seven in Points For throughout the season, but unfortunate scheduling has resulted in a 1-6 record. To put it in perspective: if Ben and Ryan had swapped schedules, Ben would be sitting at 5-2 while Ryan would be at 0-7 (apologies, Ryan). Despite the tough luck, I've ranked Ben at #13 this week due to his 60-point performance and the slim chance he has to make the playoffs. Given that Ben has more Points For than half the league, there's still a chance for him to secure a spot, although it will demand a fair bit of luck.

teams.synopsis: One of the roughest six-week stretches in league history — Ekeler, Ridley, and Lawrence all underperforming.
teams.blurb: No surprise here — Quin finds himself ranked at the bottom once again. He hasn't managed to score more than 84 points since Week 1, making this one of the roughest six-week stretches in PFFL history. With a 1-6 record, the playoff prospects are looking dim, and he might soon be competing just to avoid finishing last. The team has been a source of disappointment, with underperforming players like <mark class="hl-player">Austin Ekeler</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Calvin Ridley</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Trevor Lawrence</mark>. While some may argue Quin has been unlucky with the underwhelming production, the lack of trades in Weeks 4-6 hasn't helped his situation.
